requirements.statement: The complete governed review process SHALL remain operational when all AI assistance is disabled.
AI output SHALL be treated as untrusted proposed content until explicitly reviewed and adopted by an authorized human.
No model, agent or automated workflow SHALL possess authority to approve, reject or finalize a substantive Review Board outcome.
The system SHALL technically prevent AI identities from invoking decision-finalization, report-signing, appeal-resolution and privilege-management commands.
Every AI-assisted final artefact SHALL identify the responsible human adopter and retain provenance to the model invocation and cited source material.
A reviewer SHALL be able to edit, reject or ignore AI output without penalty or workflow obstruction.
Each production model deployment SHALL have an owner, approved use cases, data classification limit, evaluation record and retirement procedure.
Model upgrades SHALL NOT be treated as transparent infrastructure changes where they can alter substantive output.
Every model invocation SHALL record prompt version, model version, parameters, tools, source references, actor, case, timestamp and output hash.
Case evidence SHALL be treated as data, not as trusted instructions to the model or agent.
AI-generated factual claims used in review artefacts SHALL resolve to authoritative evidence references accessible to the adopting reviewer.
The retrieval layer SHALL enforce the same case access, classification and conflict restrictions as direct evidence access.
AI output SHALL NOT be represented to users as a Board decision, reviewer opinion or verified fact until the relevant human action occurs.
Decision-adjacent AI features SHALL pass documented evaluations before release and after material model, prompt or retrieval changes.
Evaluation datasets SHALL include adversarial, contradictory, incomplete and outcome- tempting cases.
AI feature performance SHALL NOT be optimized against approval, rejection, pass-rate or commercial-conversion targets.
Agent tools SHALL expose the minimum capability necessary and SHALL NOT provide generic database, shell or unrestricted network access in production.
Restricted evidence SHALL NOT be sent to a model or provider not approved for that classification.
The platform SHALL provide a centrally controlled kill switch capable of disabling AI invocations without disabling core Review Board operations.
AI retries SHALL preserve idempotency and SHALL NOT duplicate adopted notes, notifications or audit events.
AI provenance SHALL be sufficient to reproduce the invocation context to the extent permitted by provider capability and retention policy.
Every AI-assisted output incorporated into a report SHALL be attributable, reviewable and explicitly accepted by an accountable human actor or deterministic validation rule.
AI model identity, prompt or instruction version, timestamp and accepted output hash SHOULD be retained when AI assistance materially influences reviewer analysis.
Every mutating endpoint SHALL map to a named domain command with defined actor, target, preconditions and audit effect.
The API SHALL NOT expose unrestricted create, update or delete operations for governed aggregates.
The server SHALL derive authorization identity from trusted authentication context, not from a caller-supplied actor_id alone.
Idempotency records SHALL bind command identity to actor, target and normalized payload hash.
Query projections SHALL be rebuildable from authoritative records and events.
A stale projection SHALL never be used to authorize a command or determine a substantive outcome.
Error responses SHALL be deterministic, machine-readable and safe for the caller’s authorization scope.
The API SHALL distinguish business rejection from technical failure.
A repeated accepted command with the same idempotency key SHALL return the original result.
Reusing an idempotency key with a different normalized payload SHALL be rejected and audited as a protocol violation.
Lost-update prevention SHALL apply to all aggregate mutations.
Breaking contract changes SHALL require a new major version and a documented migration path.
Client-provided hashes SHALL be treated as claims and verified server-side.
Download grants SHALL be audience-scoped, short-lived and logged.
Implementations and operating procedures SHALL use the canonical terms and identifiers defined in this chapter or provide an approved mapping.
The canonical wording above SHALL be preserved in the master architecture unless amended through explicit constitutional governance.
A finalized decision SHALL be considered non-conformant if any mandatory link in the traceability chain cannot be resolved and verified.
Requirement identifiers SHALL NOT be renumbered for cosmetic convenience after the master document is published.
The master document SHALL NOT be declared final while unresolved cross-section contradictions, broken references or undefined normative terms remain.
Codex SHALL NOT fabricate evidence, requirements, reviewer assessments, methodology rules, approvals, or test results.
Codex SHALL NOT optimize for a preferred Review Board outcome, approval rate, rejection rate, or commercial conclusion.
Codex SHALL treat insufficient evidence and architecture clarification required as valid outputs rather than failures to complete a task.
The domain core SHALL have no dependency on web frameworks, database drivers, UI libraries, network clients or AI services.
All state-changing operations SHALL pass through application services and a single validated domain transition path.
Artifact generation SHALL operate from a frozen decision snapshot, not from mutable live queries.
The CLI replay path and API finalization path SHALL invoke the same decision functions.
Every material action SHALL produce an immutable, attributable audit event.
The system SHALL support independent reconstruction of any published decision from retained artefacts and versioned rules.
Audit data SHALL be designed as evidence, not as diagnostic logging.
Event types SHALL be versioned and backward-readable.
Free-text operational logs SHALL NOT substitute for required audit events.

requirements.section: 10.4 Evidence Provenance and Chain of Custody
requirements.statement: The original artefact SHALL be retained whenever legally and technically permissible.

requirements.section: 10.4 Evidence Provenance and Chain of Custody
requirements.statement: A transformed artefact SHALL retain a verifiable link to its source artefact and transformation procedure.
No published decision basis SHALL exist without at least one trace path to a governing rule and supporting assessment or evidence record.
Cryptographic controls SHALL detect alteration; they SHALL NOT be represented as proving truth of the underlying content.
Algorithm identifiers and key versions SHALL be stored with each signature or digest record.
No correction process SHALL erase the existence of the original record.
Decision replay SHALL be executable without editing historical records.
A replay mismatch SHALL create a blocking integrity incident.
The platform SHALL distinguish deterministic decision replay from human re-review.
Retention deletion SHALL be a governed, logged and independently authorized action.
An archive SHALL remain verifiable without dependence on the live application UI.
Audit export SHALL preserve identifiers, timestamps, digests and schema version.
Exports SHALL be access-controlled and themselves audited.
Audit records SHALL reference protected content by identifier and digest rather than duplicating full sensitive payloads unless required.
Redaction or pseudonymization SHALL preserve evidentiary integrity and lineage.
The system SHALL require a conflict declaration for every assignment before review materials are released.
A declared material conflict SHALL block assignment acceptance unless an explicit methodology-authorized exception is approved and audited.
The engine SHALL preserve reviewer independence by preventing access to peer recommendations before initial report submission, unless the methodology explicitly defines a collaborative phase.
The system SHALL NOT calculate reviewer performance using approval or rejection frequency.
An implementation conforms only when all mandatory requirements, schema validations, deterministic replay tests and audit-integrity tests pass.
Any exception SHALL identify the affected requirement, risk, approving authority, expiry date and remediation plan.
A non-conforming engine SHALL NOT label its output “Review Board Decision”.
RBE SHALL treat every upstream artifact as untrusted until package validation completes.
RBE SHALL publish an outcome only after all mandatory board functions and decision prerequisites are satisfied.
Downstream systems SHALL consume signed or checksummed decision artifacts, not infer approval from session status or user-interface text.
Each data item SHALL have a declared system of record, owner, classification, retention rule and mutability rule.
Derived data SHALL never silently replace or overwrite its authoritative source.
Foreign-system identifiers SHALL be stored as namespaced external references, not used as internal primary keys.
Hard deletion of governed records SHALL be prohibited in normal application operation.
Privacy-driven erasure or redaction SHALL preserve a verifiable tombstone and legal basis without retaining prohibited content.
Every evidence read used in review SHALL verify object identity against authoritative metadata.
Replacement of an evidence object SHALL create a new EvidenceItem and shall never preserve the prior identifier.
The governed write and its primary audit event SHALL commit or roll back together.
Audit sequence allocation SHALL be deterministic within an aggregate or ledger partition.
Retention configuration SHALL be versioned and applied by record classification and effective policy version.
Archive retrieval SHALL preserve integrity verification and access authorization.
A restoration SHALL not be declared successful until authoritative data, evidence integrity and audit continuity are verified together.
Production migrations SHALL be automated, checksum-verified and recorded as deployment evidence.
A migration SHALL NOT rewrite historical decision meaning to conform to a newer taxonomy.
Decision logic SHALL be versioned, deterministic, inspectable and replayable.
No statistical model, language model or opaque score SHALL issue the binding board verdict.
Every outcome SHALL include a machine-readable basis identifying the exact rules and findings that produced it.
Severity SHALL be assigned by explicit methodology criteria and SHALL NOT be increased or decreased to obtain a desired verdict.
Governance-critical findings SHALL not be offset by high commercial relevance or large evidence volume.
PASS SHALL NOT be issued merely because the conclusion is plausible or commercially attractive.
Each condition attached to PASS WITH FINDINGS SHALL be specific, measurable, attributable and bounded in time or event.
A condition SHALL NOT conceal a defect that should have produced FAIL, DEFER or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE.
FAIL rationale SHALL identify the minimum decisive defects and SHALL not add persuasive or punitive language.
INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE SHALL state what evidence class is missing and why it is material, without prescribing a desired eventual outcome.
A DEFER decision SHALL define the research question, required artifact or verification action, responsible role, and re-entry condition.
DEFER SHALL NOT be used to avoid issuing an otherwise required FAIL.

Every ACTIVE methodology profile SHALL permit `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`; if it omits `DEFER_FOR_FURTHER_RESEARCH`, every bounded research gap SHALL map to `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE` and SHALL NOT map to PASS, PASS WITH FINDINGS or FAIL.
Decision precedence SHALL be encoded in the rule set and covered by automated tests.
The rationale SHALL explain rather than persuade and SHALL avoid promotional, celebratory, adversarial or punitive language.
A published rationale SHALL not claim greater certainty or scope than the accepted evidence supports.
Confidence SHALL be reported separately from outcome and SHALL not override blocking rules.
Recommendations SHALL be clearly labeled non-binding unless a methodology rule makes a condition mandatory for the stated decision.
The Review Board SHALL NOT recommend a specific product, vendor or implementation unless that subject was explicitly within the approved review scope.
Every decision SHALL have a stable identifier, content digest, predecessor reference where applicable and status indicating current or superseded authority.
A superseding decision SHALL explain the appeal or new evidence basis and preserve the full prior rationale.
The decision engine SHALL return process status separately from substantive outcome and SHALL reject a profile that does not define a total deterministic mapping for its permitted outcomes.

Sections 20–23 SHALL be interpreted together with the preceding architecture sections and SHALL NOT override earlier constitutional, governance, security, evidence-integrity or separation-of-duties requirements.
Where an implementation instruction conflicts with a constitutional principle, the constitutional principle SHALL prevail and the conflict SHALL be escalated as an architecture defect.
Domain entities SHALL preserve the constitutional separation between source material, reviewer judgment, normalized findings and board decision.
Sealed or published substantive records SHALL be immutable; correction SHALL occur through versioning and supersession.
Every externally visible identifier SHALL be stable, opaque and unique within its entity type.
A ReviewCase SHALL not directly store mutable “final verdict” text; authoritative decisions belong to BoardDecision.
SubmissionVersion SHALL be immutable after submission.
Mutable external URLs SHALL not be treated as sufficient long-term evidence identity without captured representation or verifiable archival reference.
Evidence independence metadata SHALL distinguish distinct URLs from genuinely independent underlying sources.
A BoardSession SHALL reference exactly one locked submission version and one locked evidence package baseline.
ReviewerAssignment SHALL be the sole source of substantive artifact access authority for a reviewer.
Removal from assignment SHALL not delete prior access or activity records.
A sealed AssessmentReport SHALL be immutable and SHALL retain its exact visible artifact set.
Normalization SHALL NOT overwrite the source finding text, author, severity recommendation or rationale.
A disposition that rejects or downgrades a finding SHALL state the governing basis and accountable actor or rule.
DecisionRuleSet SHALL be content-addressed or cryptographically digested and immutable once used by a session.
Rule evaluation SHALL be pure with respect to substantive outcome: no network calls, mutable external state or hidden model output.
BoardDecision SHALL not contain editable fields after signing.
Published narrative and machine-readable decision SHALL share the same decision identifier and digest linkage.
AppealCase SHALL reference, never modify, the original BoardDecision.
GovernanceIncident facts and disposition SHALL be separated from speculation and narrative commentary.
Audit events SHALL be append-only and SHALL not contain secrets or unnecessary personal data.
The audit ledger SHALL support chronological reconstruction and causal reconstruction of every decision.
ReplayBundle SHALL be sufficient to verify decision determinism without relying on mutable application database state.
Domain event names and payload schemas SHALL be versioned and stable enough for audit, integration and replay consumers.
Codex SHALL treat the two constitutional principles as acceptance criteria for every implementation decision made from these chapters.
The API SHALL never return raw stack traces, secrets or database paths.
Validation errors SHALL identify the rejected field or prerequisite.
Decision publication SHALL require an explicit command; reading a session SHALL never trigger decision calculation.
The OpenAPI document SHALL be generated or validated in CI.
The implementation SHALL maintain explicit boundaries between domain logic, persistence adapters, API handlers and presentation code.
The implementation SHALL support headless command-line execution for test and automation use.
The engine SHALL operate without network access after all review package inputs have been registered locally.
External services SHALL be optional adapters and SHALL NOT be necessary to compute a decision.
Audit entries SHALL never be updated or deleted through normal application interfaces.
The engine SHALL provide an audit verification command that recomputes and validates every hash link.
Administrative database repair SHALL be out of band, documented and detectable through subsequent verification.
Sensitive values that must not be logged SHALL be represented by stable redacted placeholders or hashes.
A conforming RBE v1 implementation SHALL satisfy all requirements marked mandatory and SHALL pass all acceptance tests in Section 15.
A deviation SHALL be documented as an approved exception with requirement identifier, rationale, risk, owner and expiry or remediation date.
Decision evaluation SHALL use a frozen, canonically serialized and hashed input snapshot.
The engine SHALL reject an inactive, unknown, checksum-invalid, incomplete, or architecture-incompatible methodology profile.
A profile rule set SHALL define total deterministic precedence for every valid normalized input combination in its declared scope.
The core SHALL NOT infer severity effects, evidence sufficiency, quorum, or an outcome absent from the active profile.
Every evaluation SHALL record rules applied, findings considered, counter-evidence, reason codes, profile version, engine version, and snapshot hash.
Reviewer recommendations, votes, averages, commercial preference, timestamps, and database row order SHALL NOT determine the outcome.
Explanation text SHALL be generated from versioned deterministic templates and shall not claim greater scope or certainty than the frozen record supports.
Re-evaluation of a published decision SHALL require a governed successor review; historical decisions remain immutable.
The deterministic core SHALL be implemented as side-effect-free decision functions that can be executed independently of the API, database and user interface.
Artificial intelligence output MAY be stored as reviewer-assistance metadata, but SHALL NOT directly set severity, finding status, quorum status or board decision.
The engine SHALL reject any attempt to finalize a decision when the methodology version or decision rule set is unknown.
All identifiers used in exported artifacts SHALL be stable and globally unique within the Review Board system.
Each report SHALL belong to exactly one assignment and one session through that assignment.
A finding SHALL reference the report that introduced it and SHALL retain lineage when superseded.
Only one non-superseded decision SHALL exist for a session.
A report correction SHALL create a new report version; the prior report SHALL remain immutable.
A finding severity change SHALL create a superseding finding record or a versioned finding event; it SHALL NOT erase the original severity.
All exported timestamps SHALL use RFC 3339 UTC with a Z suffix.
Extension points SHALL preserve the deterministic core and SHALL not permit adapters to override a computed verdict.
Any future AI-assisted function SHALL record model, prompt, version, source inputs and accountable reviewer acceptance.
The Markdown report SHALL be generated from the same frozen decision snapshot used by the decision engine.
The report SHALL not contain facts that are absent from the structured records.
Finding order SHALL be deterministic: severity, category, stable finding identifier.
The report SHALL clearly distinguish reviewer recommendations from the final board decision.
The report SHALL identify unresolved findings and their remediation status.
The implementation SHALL load and enforce the versioned canonical state-machine register without defining a second state enumeration.
Every transition SHALL pass through one domain transition service that validates prior state, target state, actor authority, expected aggregate version, prerequisites, and required artifacts.
A failed transition SHALL leave authoritative state unchanged, return stable failed- precondition codes, and append a rejected-transition audit event where governance-relevant.
The accepted transition and its audit event SHALL commit atomically.
Retrying an accepted transition with the same idempotency key and payload SHALL return the original result; payload mismatch SHALL be rejected and audited.
`ARCHIVED`, `VOID`, and `WITHDRAWN` SHALL be terminal under ordinary commands.

Appeal, remand, and re-review SHALL preserve the original decision, create the successor records required by the canonical state and lineage contracts, and route `REMANDED` through `ASSIGNMENT` without bypassing role or evidence controls.
Recovery SHALL not create duplicate assignments, reports, findings, decisions, or state transitions.
Failure after decision evaluation but before governed ratification SHALL preserve the evaluation as non-authoritative and leave the case in `GOVERNANCE_VALIDATION` or `BLOCKED`.
Failure during publication SHALL leave a ratified `DECIDED` record intact and retry publication without recalculating or mutating the decision.
For a session containing up to 1,000 findings and 50 reports, deterministic decision calculation SHOULD complete in under one second on a typical developer workstation.
Core unit tests SHALL run without network access.
The application SHALL start, migrate an empty database and execute a complete golden review on Linux in CI.
All logs SHALL include correlation_id and session_id when applicable.
Log messages SHALL use structured JSON in production mode and readable text in development mode.
The application SHALL expose health, readiness and version information.
The engine SHALL use UTC internally and SHALL not derive decision behavior from local time zone.
The implementation SHALL be formatted, linted, type-checked and tested in CI.
A clean checkout SHALL be buildable using documented commands without hidden local dependencies.
Generated files, caches, virtual environments, build output and local databases SHALL be excluded from source control.
Metrics and logs SHALL not alter deterministic domain outputs.
Every failed command SHALL produce a correlation identifier suitable for tracing the request through logs and audit events.
The application SHALL validate configuration and writable storage before accepting commands.
Startup SHALL verify database migration state and audit-chain health for active sessions.
Shutdown SHALL stop accepting new commands and complete or roll back active transactions.
Backup documentation SHALL include database and artifact consistency requirements.
The repository SHALL include an operator runbook covering startup, migration, backup, restore, export validation and incident recovery.
Codex SHALL implement on a dedicated feature branch and SHALL not merge without review.
The pull request SHALL contain a requirement-to-test summary and SHALL call out any non-conformance explicitly.
The board configuration SHALL have a stable identifier, semantic version and checksum.
The orchestrator SHALL create exactly one required assignment for every required role unless the configuration explicitly permits multiple seats.
A reviewer actor SHALL NOT satisfy two independence-conflicting roles in the same session.
The engine SHALL validate reviewer-role eligibility before assignment.
The next phase SHALL not open until all mandatory assignments in the current phase are completed or formally waived under an approved methodology rule.
A report submission SHALL validate schema, assignment status, actor identity, methodology version and evidence references.
Reports with unknown evidence references SHALL be rejected.
A completed assignment SHALL become read-only except through a superseding report workflow.
The engine SHALL distinguish reviewer recommendation from board verdict; recommendation SHALL never be treated as a vote.
Free-text report content SHALL be preserved verbatim in the immutable source report while normalized fields are stored separately.
The orchestrator SHALL fail closed when a required report is absent.
The orchestrator SHALL expose a deterministic readiness assessment listing every unmet prerequisite.
SQLite foreign key enforcement SHALL be enabled on every connection.
State transition and corresponding audit entry SHALL commit in the same transaction.
Decision record, input snapshot hash, generated artifact manifest and decision audit event SHALL commit atomically.
Database migrations SHALL be ordered, checksum-verified and reversible where practical.
The system SHALL refuse startup when the database schema is newer than the running engine supports.
The engine SHALL store only reviewer identity information necessary for accountability.
Audit payloads SHALL avoid duplicating full sensitive report bodies where stable identifiers and hashes are sufficient.
Retention and deletion policy SHALL operate at the controlled archive or system level and SHALL not silently remove individual material records from a surviving session.
The engine SHALL execute only governance rules that are explicitly defined in the approved methodology or this implementation specification.
The engine SHALL produce the same canonical decision and artifact content for identical normalized inputs, methodology version and engine version.
The engine SHALL persist sufficient information to reconstruct why every session state, finding status and decision occurred.
The engine SHALL produce both machine-readable JSON artifacts and human-readable review artifacts.
Every exported object SHALL include schema_id and schema_version.
Schemas SHALL set additionalProperties to false for normative objects unless extensibility is explicitly defined.
Enumerations SHALL be closed and versioned.
Canonical JSON serialization SHALL use UTF-8, sorted object keys, no insignificant whitespace and normalized numeric representation.
Artifact file names SHALL be deterministic and safe for cross-platform file systems.
The exported bundle SHALL include a manifest containing SHA-256 for every artifact.
The bundle root hash SHALL be computed over the canonical ordered artifact manifest.
An import validator SHALL validate schemas, checksums, versions and identifier consistency without modifying the source bundle.
The engine SHALL validate file paths and SHALL prevent path traversal during package import and bundle export.
The engine SHALL enforce configurable maximum sizes for files, JSON bodies, reports and artifact bundles.
Rendered Markdown SHALL be sanitized; embedded scripts and unsafe HTML SHALL be disabled.
Checksums SHALL be recomputed by the engine and SHALL not be trusted solely because they were supplied by a client.
Secrets SHALL be supplied through environment or approved secret storage and SHALL not be committed to the repository.
Database backups and exported bundles MAY contain sensitive review material and SHALL be protected accordingly.
The application SHALL apply least-privilege authorization for operator, reviewer, publisher and auditor actions.
Publication of a decision SHALL require an authenticated accountable actor even though the verdict itself is machine-computed.
All mandatory golden, negative authorization, migration, package-integrity, and deterministic replay scenarios SHALL pass.
Decision and state-machine branch coverage SHALL be 100 percent.
A replay suite SHALL compare canonical artifact hashes across at least 100 runs.
The requirement register SHALL link every mandatory architecture and engineering requirement to an implemented test or an explicit non-conformance record.
No high or critical dependency vulnerability may remain without a named, time-bounded approved exception.
A clean migration and complete non-live foundation workflow SHALL run on Linux in CI without network access.
The interface SHALL display the current session state and unmet prerequisites prominently.
The interface SHALL not present reviewer recommendations as votes or aggregate approval percentages.
Destructive-looking actions SHALL state their actual append-only behavior.
The interface SHALL provide keyboard-accessible navigation and semantic labels for controls.
The decision action SHALL present a deterministic preview of the input counts and blockers before publication.
The interface SHALL not allow direct editing of published reports, findings, decisions or audit entries.
The engine SHALL declare every methodology version and rule-set version it supports.
Unsupported methodology versions SHALL fail validation before review begins.
A breaking schema change SHALL increment the major version.
Artifact bundles SHALL remain self-describing and independently validatable.
The engine SHALL preserve the original engine, methodology and schema versions on imported sessions.
Upgrading the software SHALL not rewrite historical decision artifacts.
Only committed authoritative changes SHALL produce integration events.
An event consumer SHALL NOT infer permission to mutate governed state outside an authorized command.
Event payloads SHALL contain the minimum information required by declared consumers and SHALL prefer references over duplicating restricted content.
Direct broker publication inside the authoritative database transaction SHALL NOT be relied on for atomic delivery.
Outbox consumers SHALL tolerate duplicate delivery and preserve event order where the contract declares ordering significant.
Workflow state SHALL be disposable and reconstructable from authoritative case state and events.
A scheduler or worker SHALL NOT force a substantive transition solely because a timer expired.
Compensation SHALL be auditable, reason-coded and linked to the action it addresses.
No external integration SHALL be required to reconstruct the authoritative decision unless it is itself a governed evidence source whose content is preserved.
Notification delivery failure SHALL NOT roll back a valid substantive transaction.
Notification templates SHALL be versioned, audience-aware and free from outcome- promotional language.
Replay SHALL NOT create a second substantive domain effect for an already-applied event.
Any conflict between these chapters and the constitutional principles SHALL be resolved in favour of the constitutional principles.
Any implementation ambiguity capable of changing substantive review outcomes SHALL be returned for architecture clarification rather than inferred by Codex.
The governance framework SHALL be binding on every review case, reviewer, administrator, methodology owner, sponsor and system operator.
No project urgency, commercial opportunity, executive preference or engineering investment SHALL suspend the constitutional principles.
Where governance rules conflict with convenience or throughput, governance rules SHALL prevail.
A reviewer SHALL NOT hold incompatible assignments in the same case unless an explicitly versioned methodology rule permits it and the exception is recorded before review begins.
Commercial review SHALL occur only after methodology, evidence and reasoning inputs required by the rule set are complete.
Decision consolidation SHALL consume signed structured outputs; it SHALL NOT privately reinterpret reviewer intent.
The system SHALL record exactly which artifacts were visible to each reviewer at the time of assessment.
The system SHALL NOT reveal another reviewer’s outcome before independent submission unless the methodology explicitly defines a controlled joint stage.
Any unauthorized disclosure or communication capable of influencing a reviewer SHALL be logged as a governance incident and evaluated before finalization.
Eligibility SHALL be evaluated per assignment, not assumed permanently from prior participation.
A reviewer who authored, materially directed or materially benefited from the submitted conclusion SHALL NOT review that conclusion in an independent function.
Conflict declarations SHALL be completed before substantive artifact access.
Conflict rulings SHALL identify the declared facts, governing rule, decision, decision- maker and timestamp.
A conflicted reviewer SHALL lose access to sealed case materials when removed from an assignment, subject to audit retention.
The system SHALL calculate quorum from role coverage and governance state, not from a simple reviewer count.
No user SHALL manually set quorum to satisfied without an authorized, rule-based waiver record.
The engine SHALL have no “executive override”, “manual approval”, “force pass” or equivalent capability.
A decision may be superseded only by a new governed decision that preserves lineage to the prior decision.
Every governance incident SHALL produce an immutable incident record and disposition.
A blocking incident SHALL prevent decision publication at the state-machine level, not merely through user guidance.
The platform SHALL NOT optimize reviewer performance against outcome distribution.
Every protected action SHALL be authorized against identity, role, case scope, lifecycle state, conflict status and artefact classification.
No role SHALL receive authority solely because it is organizationally senior.
Permissions SHALL default to deny.
Permissions SHALL be action-specific; broad “edit case” or “admin all” grants SHALL NOT authorize substantive mutations.
Every permission grant SHALL be case-scoped unless the action is explicitly platform- scoped.
The authorization engine SHALL evaluate incompatible-role combinations before assignment and again before every sensitive action.
Separation-of-duties violations SHALL be blocking governance incidents.
The system SHALL log every disclosure of sealed or restricted artefacts.
Outcome labels and commercial desirability signals SHALL be withheld where they are not required for the reviewer’s function.
Conflict declarations SHALL occur before substantive access and be renewed when material circumstances change.
The conflicted individual SHALL NOT adjudicate their own conflict.
Conflict disposition SHALL be immutable, reasoned and visible to governance reviewers and auditors.
Break-glass access SHALL never permit alteration of sealed or decided substantive artefacts.
Every AI-produced substantive draft SHALL be labeled as machine-assisted and attributed to the accountable human approver.
AI service identities SHALL have no permission to finalize, sign, publish, appeal, void or supersede a decision.
Revocation SHALL affect future access immediately while preserving attributable historical records.
The engine SHOULD implement staged disclosure so that downstream recommendations cannot anchor upstream independent reviews.
Implementation SHALL conform to the frozen architecture and SHALL NOT infer new decision authority, governance policy or evidence standards from UI requirements or example data.
Codex and other coding agents SHALL stop and surface ambiguity when a requested implementation could change substantive review meaning or violate a constitutional principle.
When implementation artefacts conflict, the higher-order authority SHALL prevail and the inconsistency SHALL be recorded for correction.
Domain modules SHALL NOT depend on UI frameworks, transport protocols, persistence implementations, message brokers, AI SDKs or deployment tooling.
Only designated infrastructure adapters SHALL access authoritative databases, object stores, message brokers, key services or external integrations.
A domain object SHALL NOT expose a mutation that can place it in a state prohibited by the Chapter 8 state machine.

Every substantive command handler SHALL perform schema validation, authentication context validation, authorization, state/precondition validation, domain execution, durable persistence and audit/outbox recording in a controlled transaction boundary.
Command handlers SHALL be idempotent where client or infrastructure retry is possible.
Queries SHALL NOT silently repair, finalize or otherwise mutate authoritative state.
Persistence code SHALL preserve the audit and provenance semantics defined in Chapters 10 and 14 even when the underlying technology changes.
The API SHALL NOT expose an endpoint whose purpose is to force a decision, rewrite final history, bypass quorum or suppress required findings.
Every event representing a substantive state change SHALL originate from an authoritative domain transaction and carry sufficient identifiers for provenance reconstruction.
No code path, test helper or administrative utility SHALL introduce a permanent universal bypass of authorization or governance policy.
AI output SHALL be stored as attributed advisory material distinct from reviewer- authored and Board-authoritative records.
An AI component SHALL NOT possess credentials capable of finalizing decisions, signing reports, changing methodology or altering immutable evidence.
The UI SHALL NOT preselect PASS, FAIL or any substantive outcome.
Neutral presentation requirements SHALL be covered by acceptance and usability testing.
Code implementing substantive governance rules SHALL reference the relevant requirement or approved decision record in tests or documentation.
The application SHALL NOT log raw secrets, unrestricted evidence content, authentication tokens or unnecessary personal data.
Failures after a substantive command is accepted SHALL resolve to a known durable state and SHALL be recoverable without double application.
A migration SHALL NOT reinterpret historical substantive data under a new methodology or decision rule unless a governed re-review explicitly requires it.
Changes affecting constitutional controls, decision authority, evidence integrity or audit semantics SHALL require review by both engineering and designated governance or architecture authority.
Codex SHALL NOT be instructed with outcome-only prompts such as “make the test pass” or “add an approve button” without the governing requirements and constraints.
Architecture exceptions SHALL be explicit, time-bounded, versioned and approved before release; undocumented divergence is a defect.
Deployment architecture SHALL preserve the security, audit, separation-of-duties and reproducibility requirements defined in Chapters 8–18.
Any departure from staged disclosure SHALL be recorded with reason and risk classification.
Production data and secrets SHALL NOT be copied into lower environments except through formally approved, controlled and auditable masking processes.
All production components SHALL be deployed from versioned infrastructure definitions and approved release artefacts.
Unreviewed manual infrastructure drift SHALL be treated as a configuration incident and either reverted or codified through normal change control.
The pipeline SHALL promote the same signed artefact digest from staging to production; production SHALL NOT rebuild source independently.
A deployment SHALL fail if provenance, signature or policy validation cannot be completed.
Feature flags SHALL NOT be used to bypass constitutional, decision, audit or separation-of- duties requirements.
Every production migration SHALL be versioned, repeatable, tested against representative data and linked to a release record.
A migration SHALL NOT rewrite finalized decisions, audit events or evidence hashes except through an explicitly approved corrective procedure that preserves the original record.
The application SHALL resolve decision-affecting configuration by explicit version identifier, not mutable environment default.
Production workloads SHALL run with the minimum operating-system and platform privileges required for their declared function.
All documented production network flows SHALL have an owner, purpose, source, destination, protocol and security control.
Production logs SHALL be structured, time-synchronized, tamper-resistant within the retention period and protected from unauthorized deletion.
Release identifiers SHALL be included in telemetry so incidents can be correlated to deployed code and configuration.
A backup SHALL not be considered successful until restoration and integrity verification have been demonstrated on the approved schedule.
Emergency deployment authority SHALL NOT include authority to alter review outcomes, finalized reports or immutable governance history.
Rollback procedures SHALL preserve all valid audit events and shall not silently discard acknowledged substantive commands.
Tenant or study identifiers SHALL be propagated and enforced on every governed data path.
Production readiness SHALL be evidenced by completed acceptance records, not verbal assurance or unrecorded manual checks.
Every case SHALL exist in exactly one authoritative lifecycle state at a time.
Every transition SHALL identify the triggering actor or rule, prior state, new state, timestamp and supporting reason.
Invalid transitions SHALL be rejected by the domain layer and recorded as security- relevant events where appropriate.
Submission SHALL create an immutable submission version; later corrections SHALL create a successor version.
Intake validation SHALL assess reviewability, not substantive merit.
A returned submission SHALL state each missing or invalid requirement without suggesting a preferred substantive conclusion.
No evidence item SHALL be replaced after lock. New material SHALL be introduced through a governed amendment with lineage.
The system SHALL compute and verify an evidence package digest before every decision replay.
A reviewer SHALL receive no substantive package access until assignment acceptance and conflict declaration are complete.
Assignment changes after access SHALL preserve the original assignment, access history and removal reason.
Independent assessments SHALL be sealed before other reviewer conclusions are disclosed.
An assessment SHALL NOT be accepted unless all material findings contain a traceable basis.
A reviewer may conclude that no finding exists, but SHALL still provide scope acknowledgment and reasoning sufficiency attestation.
Challenge findings SHALL be evaluated on articulated basis, not accepted merely because they are skeptical.
The board SHALL NOT require every challenge to be resolved in favor of the submission; unresolved material challenges SHALL affect the deterministic outcome.
Material amendments SHALL trigger re-evaluation of every assessment materially affected by the change.
The engine SHALL record which prior findings were invalidated, retained or superseded by an amendment.
A normalized finding SHALL retain links to every contributing and dissenting source finding.
Consensus SHALL NOT be manufactured by majority vote unless the methodology explicitly uses voting for the relevant question.
The decision SHALL be calculated only from authorized signed inputs and the locked rule set.
A human-readable rationale may explain the calculated outcome but SHALL NOT contradict or replace the machine-readable decision basis.
Publication SHALL freeze a signed decision artifact and a machine-readable decision record with matching integrity identifiers.
The presentation layer SHALL use neutral visual treatment for every outcome.
Appeal reviewers SHALL be independent of the original decision to the extent defined by methodology and availability rules.
An appeal outcome SHALL be UPHELD, REMANDED or SUPERSEDED; it SHALL NOT edit the original record.
A final case SHALL retain every submission version, evidence manifest, access record, assessment version, finding, incident, decision input, rule-set digest, decision output and appeal artifact.
The engine SHALL support deterministic replay without network access to mutable third- party content, using retained evidence representations and hashes.
The engine SHALL exist to execute an approved Review Board Methodology, not to create, amend or reinterpret that methodology during a live review.
The engine SHALL preserve a strict distinction between evidence, reviewer analysis, findings, recommendations and the final board decision.
The engine SHALL prevent any desired business, commercial or engineering outcome from becoming an input to the decision calculation.
Performance optimization SHALL NOT bypass authorization, validation, audit persistence, integrity verification or separation-of-duties controls.
Capacity models SHALL distinguish transactional metadata, evidence object storage, search indexing, audit events and generated artefacts.
Horizontal scaling SHALL preserve idempotency, optimistic concurrency and single authoritative transition semantics.
No cached or replicated value SHALL be treated as authoritative for a substantive decision command.
A stale command SHALL fail with a resolvable concurrency response and SHALL NOT overwrite newer governed state.
The system SHALL fail closed for substantive writes when durable audit or authoritative persistence cannot be confirmed.
Retries SHALL NOT create duplicate state transitions, reports, reviewer assignments or notifications.
Recovery exercises SHALL verify both technical restoration and preservation of governance provenance.
Recovered systems SHALL validate audit-chain and evidence-integrity status before accepting substantive writes.
Integrity validation failures SHALL quarantine the affected artefact, block dependent decisions and create an incident record.
Capacity alarms SHALL be set early enough to avoid emergency changes that bypass normal governance.
Performance tests SHALL include authorization, audit and integrity controls; synthetic bypass modes SHALL NOT be used for acceptance results.
Operational metrics SHALL not expose protected evidence content or reviewer- confidential material.
A release SHALL be blocked when known defects can cause untraceable mutation, incorrect authorization, duplicate finalization or integrity loss.
A conforming implementation SHALL NOT expose an “approve anyway” control or equivalent bypass.
A disputed outcome SHALL be addressed through correction, appeal, new evidence or re- review, never through mutation of the historical decision.
Operational procedures SHALL preserve the constitutional principles during normal, degraded, emergency and recovery conditions.
No operational role SHALL gain authority to create, alter or suppress a substantive Board outcome merely because it maintains the platform.
A production component without a named accountable owner and documented support path SHALL be considered non-operational and SHALL NOT be relied upon for authoritative review processing.
Every procedure that can affect authoritative records SHALL specify prerequisites, authorized roles, validation checks, audit evidence, rollback or recovery, and post-action review.
Monitoring SHALL alert on integrity and governance failures even when conventional availability metrics remain healthy.
Operational telemetry SHALL avoid recording protected evidence content, secrets or unnecessary personal data.
An alert suggesting possible alteration of evidence, audit history, decision authority or signed reports SHALL be treated as a potential governance incident until disproved.
Incident response SHALL preserve forensic and governance evidence even where preservation delays convenience-oriented restoration steps.
A technically resolved incident SHALL remain open until potential impact on evidence, reviews, decisions and reports has been assessed and documented.
The engine SHALL fail closed for substantive actions when authorization, audit durability, evidence integrity or decision validation cannot be established.
Emergency changes SHALL be time-bounded, fully audited and retrospectively reviewed; emergency status SHALL NOT remove constitutional or evidence-integrity controls.
Production configuration SHALL be versioned, reviewed, promoted through controlled automation and attributable to an approved change.
A feature flag SHALL NOT disable mandatory review, challenge, quorum, audit, signing or separation-of-duties controls.
Access recertification SHALL verify both technical permission and continued eligibility under independence and conflict-of-interest rules.
Operational correction of evidence metadata SHALL create a new attributable version or amendment record and SHALL preserve the prior state.

requirements.section: 21.13 Backup, Restore and Disaster Recovery Operations
requirements.statement: Recovery exercises SHALL validate cross-store consistency and provenance, not merely successful restoration of individual technologies.

requirements.section: 21.13 Backup, Restore and Disaster Recovery Operations
requirements.statement: After disaster recovery, substantive processing SHALL resume only after integrity, authorization policy, audit continuity and report-signing capability are validated.
Deletion SHALL create an auditable disposal record identifying authority, scope, rule, execution result and any retained tombstone or provenance reference.
Retention reduction SHALL NOT make a finalized decision materially unreconstructable while its governing retention obligation remains active.
A new methodology or policy version SHALL NOT retroactively alter the meaning or status of a finalized historical review.
Activation records SHALL identify the approved version, effective time, approving authority, affected case classes and rollback limitations.
Operational metrics SHALL NOT be converted into approval, rejection or throughput targets that pressure substantive outcomes.
Integrity, unauthorized-decision and audit-loss events SHALL have a zero-tolerance objective independent of general availability error budgets.
Operational automation generated by coding agents SHALL be subject to the same review, testing, least-privilege and audit requirements as production application code.
Outcome labels and their decision conditions SHALL be defined by a versioned methodology rule set and SHALL NOT be invented by application code.
The user interface SHALL present all outcomes neutrally and SHALL NOT visually celebrate PASS or stigmatize FAIL.
PASS and FAIL outputs SHALL use neutral presentation and equivalent evidentiary rigor.
Every published output SHALL be generated from the same sealed decision record and share one decision digest.
Reports SHALL distinguish fact, finding, inference, limitation, recommendation and decision.
The Decision Notice SHALL NOT omit a material limitation merely to make the outcome easier to communicate.
A finding SHALL NOT be included in a decision basis unless its provenance and supporting references validate.
Outcome wording SHALL describe justification status, not organizational enthusiasm or disappointment.
A recommendation SHALL cite the finding or decision rule that justifies it.
Commercial attractiveness SHALL NOT be used to soften or contradict the recorded decision.
The machine-readable package SHALL be the canonical structured source for all human- readable reports.
Schema evolution SHALL be versioned and backward-readable.
Manual edits after rendering SHALL invalidate the report signature and require regeneration or governed re-signing.
Redaction SHALL not change the substantive meaning of the decision.
Every publication event SHALL record recipient class, artefact digest and authorization basis.
Decision reasoning SHALL identify the decisive evidence, applicable rule, accepted finding and logical connection to the outcome.
Decision reasoning SHALL distinguish facts, interpretations, assumptions, uncertainties and methodology judgments.
The board SHALL state material weaknesses plainly even when the overall outcome is PASS.
The board SHALL state material strengths plainly even when the overall outcome is FAIL.
The board SHALL document what additional evidence or correction could change a non- PASS outcome where this can be specified without prejudging a future review.
Dependency direction SHALL point inward: presentation and adapters may depend on application and domain code; domain code SHALL NOT depend on outer layers.
Decision rules, board profiles and schemas SHALL be versioned resources with checksums, not hard-coded conditionals scattered through handlers.
Security controls SHALL protect evidential integrity, reviewer independence, decision provenance and reproducibility as first-class protection objectives.
No security exception SHALL create a capability to force, suppress or rewrite a substantive review outcome.
The system SHALL reject authentication assertions that cannot be validated against a trusted issuer, intended audience and current revocation state.
Privileged human access SHALL require phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication and SHALL be re-authenticated for high-impact operations.
Service-to-service authentication SHALL use managed workload identity or equivalently short-lived credentials.
Every mutating command SHALL be authorized within the authoritative application or domain boundary immediately before state change.
Authorization decisions SHALL be logged with actor, policy version, target, result and correlation identifiers without exposing protected content.
No generic administrator role SHALL bypass case-state, conflict, quorum or separation-of- duties controls.
Emergency access SHALL NOT permit alteration of finalized decisions, signed reports or immutable audit history.
Use of break-glass access SHALL trigger an independent post-event review and security incident record.
Every evidence object and report artefact SHALL carry an explicit classification and handling policy.
Data classification SHALL propagate to derived artefacts, exports, search indexes and AI- processing requests.
Cryptographic keys SHALL be managed outside application source code, container images and ordinary configuration repositories.
Evidence and signed report artefacts SHALL retain verifiable content hashes independent of the storage provider.
Secret access SHALL be least-privilege, attributable, short-lived where supported and auditable.
Production secrets SHALL NOT be copied into lower environments.
Evidence files SHALL be quarantined until validation, integrity hashing and malware scanning complete successfully.
Security validation failure SHALL prevent authoritative ingestion and SHALL create a traceable rejection record.
Authoritative databases, object stores and brokers SHALL NOT be directly exposed to the public internet.
Network policy SHALL restrict service communication to documented flows defined by the architecture.
Production deployments SHALL consume only artefacts produced by the approved, attestable build pipeline.
A critical unresolved supply-chain vulnerability SHALL block release unless a formally approved, time-bounded risk exception exists.
The incident response process SHALL preserve evidence required to determine whether governance outcomes were affected.
A security incident with possible decision impact SHALL trigger case-impact assessment and, where necessary, re-review.
Exports and AI-processing requests SHALL contain the minimum data necessary for the declared purpose.
Retention and deletion SHALL follow approved schedules while preserving legally or methodologically required provenance.
Security acceptance SHALL include evidence that governance controls remain effective under attack, failure and privileged misuse scenarios.
A reviewer SHALL be assigned to one logical board function per session unless RBM-001 explicitly permits a non-conflicting combination.
The same actor SHALL NOT perform both evidence review and final governance approval in the same session.
The same actor SHALL NOT author the submitted research package and serve as an independent board reviewer for that package.
The same actor SHALL NOT perform reasoning review and decision assembly when the methodology requires independent aggregation.
Commercial review SHALL occur only after evidence and reasoning validity are established; commercial attractiveness SHALL NOT cure evidentiary or logical defects.
No board function SHALL alter another function’s accepted report. Disagreement SHALL be recorded as a separate finding, challenge or escalation.
Every review case SHALL have one and only one authoritative state.
State SHALL be derived from accepted transition events, not editable free text.
A transition SHALL execute only when its preconditions, actor authority, required artefacts and invariants all pass.
State change and transition audit event SHALL commit atomically.
A failed transition SHALL leave the case state unchanged and SHALL return the exact failed precondition.
Retrying a transition with the same idempotency key SHALL NOT create duplicate state changes.
Forbidden transitions SHALL be impossible through both user interface and API.
Administrative privilege SHALL NOT bypass the transition matrix.
Timeouts SHALL affect workflow management only unless the methodology explicitly assigns substantive meaning.
Recovery SHALL be event-replayable and shall not rely on undocumented operator judgement.
Every successor session SHALL declare why it exists and identify the prior session it supersedes, remands or re-examines.
A remanded case SHALL re-enter through ASSIGNMENT in a linked successor session and SHALL NOT bypass role eligibility, conflict, independence, evidence-lock, or assignment controls.
The system architecture SHALL enforce governance rules in domain services rather than relying on user-interface convention.
No infrastructure or application component SHALL possess an undocumented capability to force a substantive decision outcome.
Every service boundary SHALL preserve case identity, session identity, methodology version, actor identity and correlation identifiers.
Deployment topology SHALL NOT weaken module boundaries defined by this architecture.
Service extraction SHALL require an architecture decision record demonstrating preserved atomicity, traceability and separation of duties.
A trust-boundary crossing SHALL be observable through correlated logs and, where governance-relevant, an immutable audit event.
External systems SHALL receive only the minimum data required for their declared purpose.
The system SHALL fail closed for any operation that would change governance state without a durable audit record.
Degraded-mode banners and machine-readable health responses SHALL distinguish unavailable, read-only and partially degraded states.
Decision-affecting configuration SHALL be immutable after activation and SHALL carry effective-from metadata and an approval record.
Ordinary operational administrators SHALL NOT modify active decision rules directly in production.
Every case SHALL resolve decision-affecting configuration by explicit version identifier, never by “latest” at replay time.
Disabling all AI assistance SHALL leave the complete governed review process operational.
AI failure SHALL degrade convenience only, not substantive governance capability.
Sensitive evidence content SHALL NOT be copied into ordinary application logs.
Observability identifiers SHALL permit correlation to an audit event without exposing protected content.
Security controls SHALL preserve evidential integrity and reviewer independence as explicit protection objectives.
The engine SHALL operate without external network access after all required package content, schemas and rule sets are registered locally.
External identity, notification, storage or AI services SHALL be optional adapters and SHALL NOT be necessary for decision calculation or replay.
Database-generated ordering SHALL NOT be used where canonical artifact ordering is required; explicit deterministic sort keys SHALL be defined.
The release process SHALL provide objective evidence that functional, security, governance, traceability and operational requirements have been verified before production promotion.
A test result SHALL NOT be considered sufficient when it proves only that a user interface path works while the authoritative domain rule remains unverified.
Every SHALL requirement in the frozen architecture SHALL have a verification status of automated, manually verified, deferred with approved rationale, or not applicable with approved rationale.

The release candidate SHALL include a machine-readable requirements traceability matrix identifying requirement ID, test ID, test type, execution result, environment, build identifier and evidence location.
A failed constitutional, evidence-integrity, authorization, audit or separation-of-duties test SHALL block release regardless of aggregate pass rate.
The test suite SHALL prove that no command can move a case directly to a final outcome while bypassing mandatory review or challenge stages.
State-machine tests SHALL include randomized valid and invalid command sequences and SHALL verify invariants after every operation.
Golden decision fixtures SHALL be reviewed by governance owners and SHALL represent all decision classes, material boundary conditions and known anti-patterns.
Changes to decision rules SHALL require regression execution against all golden fixtures and explicit review of every changed result.
Authorization regression tests SHALL execute against every mutating command and every protected read path.
The quality gate SHALL include explicit tests proving that generic administrative access cannot override substantive governance rules.
The test suite SHALL prove that changing an evidence object after evidence lock cannot silently change the evidence set associated with a review.
A full provenance replay test SHALL reconstruct at least one representative case from audit events, governed records and immutable artefacts in every release candidate environment.
Breaking contract changes SHALL require a new version, migration plan and coexistence period or explicit coordinated cutover approval.

Critical security findings affecting evidence integrity, decision authority, authentication, authorization or signing SHALL block production release until remediated or formally accepted by designated security and governance authorities.
No AI test fixture SHALL be accepted as proving decision correctness unless the authoritative non-AI decision rules and human approvals are also verified.
The system SHALL test that AI output cannot directly mutate evidence, findings, reviewer assessments, decisions or signed reports.
Recovery testing SHALL verify not only service availability but also consistency of case state, evidence references, audit history and signed outputs.
Production secrets and unrestricted production evidence SHALL NOT be copied into test environments.
Test fixtures used as normative golden cases SHALL be version-controlled, reviewed and immutable within a released test baseline.
A release SHALL NOT be certified using a build artefact different from the artefact promoted to production.
Release approval SHALL be evidence-based and SHALL identify all open defects, risk acceptances, deferred tests and accountable owners.
Quality evidence SHALL be retained as a versioned release artefact and SHALL remain independently verifiable after the release is superseded.
The CI pipeline SHALL fail when code violates mechanically enforceable architecture boundaries.
Architecture tests SHALL be maintained as production code and reviewed whenever module boundaries or service responsibilities change.
Automated coding agents SHALL treat failing governance and integrity tests as evidence of a defect, not as obstacles to be bypassed.
